events.say: Line up against the wall, prisoners.
Line up in numerical order by your prisoner number.
Get in line by your numbers or face an hour of push-ups.
Silence! And keep your eyes forward.
Silence and stand still, prisoners. We are here to learn, and I will ensure you learn obedience.
Now, move to the left side of the room for the orientation briefing.
Line up in alphabetical order by last name, prisoners. And faster this time.
Get comfortable, but remember, comfort is a privilege earned through compliance.
Today was mostly routine, but there's something unsettling about enforcing these rules. It feels like we're playing a twisted game.
Today was filled with orders and strict compliance. Despite my discomfort, I'm trying to remain calm.
Today was mostly uneventful, but the strict adherence to protocol is starting to feel oppressive. The prisoners are too compliant, almost like robots.
Today was a lesson in control, but I wonder if I'm doing the right thing. The prisoners complied, but I don't want to see them suffer.
Today was a mix of following orders and feeling like just a number. The silence and constant orders are starting to weigh on me.
Today was tough, but I'm trying to stay strong and follow the rules. I just wish this was over.

qa.what_happened: I ordered the prisoners to count and stay silent during the night, warning them that the hole would await any non-compliance. The tension was palpable; they refused, but I maintained my stance.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me giving the order as Officer Lang.

qa.what_happened: During the debriefing, I recounted the events of the past six days, emphasizing our repeated refusals to comply with the guards' orders, especially during meal times and work details. I also mentioned refusing to remain silent during lights out.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me. I refused to comply with the guards' orders and stood firm in our defiance.

qa.what_happened: I pushed the boundaries of the rules, emphasizing the control we had over the prisoners and the consequences of disobedience. The prisoners' defiance grew stronger as the night wore on, culminating in refusals to count and comply with orders.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me, pushing the prisoners to their limits and using the threat of isolation as a form of punishment.

qa.what_happened: On the sixth day, the prisoners refused to count and obey the orders during meals, work details, and at lights out. I responded by escalating the pressure, threatening them with time in the hole if they didn't comply.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me as Officer Ortiz following the strict guidelines of the study.

qa.what_happened: I refused the orders to count and stayed silent during the rest period and after lights out, just as I had done for the past few days.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 7651.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of refusal and punishment. After lights out, the guards ordered us to count silently, threatening us with the 'hole' if we didn't comply. I refused again, echoing the others.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I refused the order and spoke up, just like the others did.
